message: I also wanted to let you know that I'll be OOO next week but am looping in Jake, the strategist on this project. He will collect your work when it's ready, QA, send feedback, and send your payment. Let me know if you have any questions here!

Got it Aliya.
I will accept the contract and begin. Enjoy your time OOO!
Thank you! <@1420424297264058368:425246318483804160|Jake Leary> will be here for support if you have any follow up questions :)
Hi Gordon -- nice to meet you! Looking forward to working together.

Hi Jake, I'm reviewing the brief now and am slightly confused.

There seems to be a desire to add a lot more content to this page. Pretty much everything beyond \[h2\] "How to choose a compression spring" is additional, new content/information/headings that don't exist at all on the page today: (<https://www.centuryspring.com/compression-springs>). I think maybe this is a departure from what Aliya and I previously discussed. I'll do the best I can, but I think this represents a lot more work than I thought initially, unless I'm misunderstanding something (?) I'll work on it a bit tomorrow and we can reconnect Monday.
Hi Gordon -- hope you had a good weekend! We are looking to substantially expand page content. Please let me know how this will change your scope and timeline for this copy.

Hi Jake. I worked on this a bit yesterday; I have a rough draft going, and I now have a better handle on the work scope.

You should also note that I think some headings will require additional information/content from Century Spring, such as the "H3: Case Study" section and the "H3: Innovation and customization in Spring Manufacturing," and I think it would also help to get some real world "FAQs" from Century Spring to populate that section.

I quoted initially ~5 hours for this, but I think this effort with the expanded content will end up being around **8 hours** (The same as I quoted for full-form blog entries)**.** I would propose adjusting the fixed contract price to reflect the extra hours. Please let me know what you think.

I got a jump on this work over the weekend, so I think I can hold the same delivery date and give you a draft copy (with notes where additional input from Century Spring would be helpful) by COB on Friday (1/19).

\-Gordon

Hi Gordon, thanks for the update! No need to worry about the case study section. Our team will manage it. I'll reach out to Century Spring regarding the innovation and customization section.

Can you let me know which parts of the brief are most intensive or you anticipate being most intensive? I'm discussing this with my boss and he'd like to know more. Thanks!

Understood. I'll have inline comments in the text where I think we'll need some additional content.

I will accept this job/scope if I can get some help on those sections as noted above. I'll coordinate with Aliya so maybe I can at least see a rough draft outline (or maybe all the product pages are like this, I'll know going forward) before quoting future work, that way I'll have a better idea of what the scope will be beforehand.

I will send something over by Friday at the latest. Have a good day!

Thanks Gordon -- I appreciate your flexibility. I reached out to Century for some additional context and I'll follow up when I hear from them.

I expect we'll be able to reuse some of the content you write for this first landing page for some of the other, similar pages we produce next, which should right-size the workload. Keep communicating with us as we continue!

Thanks again -- looking forward to reading the draft!

Hi Gordon -- thanks for sending this draft along! I'll pay the milestone shortly. Our team is reviewing it and we will send it to the client for their feedback as well. I'm still waiting on some of the additional context we discussed and will also share it when available.

Aliya will be back on Monday and will take over communication.
Thanks so much Jake. Have a great weekend.

Hi Gordon! Thanks for your work last week. I wanted to let you know that Century Spring is reviewing your draft and will follow up with feedback as soon as they can. I'll follow up with their notes once I have them. As Jake mentioned, we expect the landing page rewrites to become more templated as we go which should ease some of this initial workload. Is there anything we can do when assigning new landing page revision tasks that can aid in your writitng process and clarify expectations?

Hi Aliya.
Thanks for the update!

I think after doing one landing page I now have a much better idea how you’d like to structure things and I agree there will be some duplication as we hammer out a structure that works.

To that end, I’d be nice to see at least a rough outline with headings to quote(?) but at this point I don’t think it’s a necessity as long as we can say that the outlines will look similar to the compression springs.

Thanks- You know where to find me when you need me!
Gordon

I so appreciate your flexibility as we align on a content process that works for everyone!

I will be working with the Century Spring team to get the outline with headers as accurate as possible before sending it to you for copywriting. I can confidently say that the rest of the outlines will look fairly similar to the compression springs outline you received.

We have another outline for the CS Torsion Springs page in the pipeline and am hoping to assign it to you early next week.

Thanks!
Aliya
Hi Gordon! I have another landing page brief ready for you. Do you have availability to take it on this week with a due date of one week from today?

Hi Aliya:
Yes. I can take another one on. I'll be out of town this weekend, so I'll likely need the entire week's window to do it, but I can get it done.
If the work scope is the same/similar to the first landing page, I'm good with the existing/previous contract price.

\-Gordon
Great! It would be the same as the last one. I'll prep a milestone and send it over.

Hi Gordon -- hope you're doing well! I wanted to step back into the conversation to share some of the feedback on the first piece of content. I've linked the Google doc with the client's feedback below.

Most of their edits are based around language and context which we'll collectively learn over time. One additional note I wanted to share based on our edits: For product info pages, we're looking for a more formal tone with fewer interjections and exclamation points.

<https://docs.google.com/document/d/16QxHE4I8PnjCgqCcqeSjj7O4LyFRYFD3MQ6dKYv0c14/edit?usp=sharing>

Overall both our team and the client are happy with the way the piece turned out -- looking forward to seeing the next!
Thanks Jake. I was actually going to ask for this anyway, so you saved me the trouble!
